newsitem.title: ESTONIA: HANDELSBANKEN'S AKTORIS STILL BUILDS RESOURCES.
newsitem.headline: HANDELSBANKEN'S AKTORIS STILL BUILDS RESOURCES.

text.p: Aktoris, the Estonian broker recently bought by Svenska Handelsbanken, said on Friday it was still in the process of building up its resources to reach its stated aim of a 10 percent market share.
The company also said there was strong interest from foreign investors in the Baltic markets.

Aktoris is fully operational as a trader on the Tallinn stock exchange and the firm's managing director Auli Kumpulainen said Aktoris still needed to beef up its human resources to take the targetted 10 percent market share.
"We are recruiting now and we will employ four new people by the end of the year," Kumpulainen told Reuters.
"We just don't have the full human resources needed at present," she added.
She said the company also needed to hire more people to take a more active role in the markets of Latvia and Lithuania.
"Our involvement on the Latvian and Lithuanian markets is a human resources question but those markets are still of great interest."
Kumpilainen also said that foreign investor interest in the Baltics was great.
"Since the purchase of Aktoris in March, we have had strong investor interest from Handelsbanken's offices in Paris, London, New York among others," Kumpulainen added.
"Of course there is also very strong interest from Sweden and another fund recently received permission to invest with us," she added.
Svenska Handelsbanken bought Aktoris for an undisclosed price on March 24, becoming the first foreign bank to become directly active on the Estonian market.
